question: What is the main difference between fat-soluble and water-soluble vitamins in how the body handles them?

options.A: Fat-soluble vitamins are cleared rapidly through daily urination
options.B: Water-soluble vitamins pose a much higher risk of long-term toxicity
options.C: Water-soluble vitamins are stored in high amounts within the liver
options.D: Fat-soluble vitamins dissolve in lipids and accumulate in body tissues

explanation: Because fat-soluble vitamins dissolve in fats, the body stores them in the liver and adipose tissue rather than quickly excreting them through urine. [learn more](BMP118_U2_T4#BMP118_U2_T4_h1)

question: Why is maternal vitamin D intake especially important for a developing fetus?

options.A: It directly synthesizes red blood cells in the fetal bone marrow
options.B: It prevents maternal oxidative stress within the placental bed
options.C: It regulates calcium homeostasis for fetal bone mineralization
options.D: It stimulates immediate cellular differentiation of skin layers

explanation: Vitamin D controls how calcium is absorbed and used, which is vital for building strong bones and teeth in the growing fetus. [learn more](BMP118_U2_T4#BMP118_U2_T4_h1)

question: Which digestive substance is needed in the small intestine to help absorb fat-soluble vitamins?
explanation: Bile salts break down large fat globules into smaller droplets, allowing fat-soluble vitamins to be properly absorbed by the gut. [learn more](BMP118_U2_T4#BMP118_U2_T4_h2)

question: A pregnant woman has a condition that makes it hard to digest fats. What will happen to her fat-soluble vitamin levels?

options.A: Levels will fluctuate rapidly based on her daily carbohydrate intake
options.B: Levels will spike dangerously high due to improper liver storage failure
options.C: Levels will remain normal because fat malabsorption only affects water-soluble vitamins
options.D: Levels will drop because these vitamins rely on dietary fat absorption pathways

explanation: Conditions that impair fat digestion or absorption will also block the uptake of vitamins A, D, E, and K, leading to deficiency. [learn more](BMP118_U2_T4#BMP118_U2_T4_h2)

question: Which fat-soluble vitamin helps activate blood-clotting factors?
explanation: Vitamin K is essential for blood coagulation because it helps activate several clotting factors in the liver. [learn more](BMP118_U2_T4#BMP118_U2_T4_h3)

question: How does vitamin E protect maternal and fetal cells from damage?

options.A: By directly regulating the absorption of dietary calcium
options.B: By neutralizing free radicals as a lipid-soluble antioxidant
options.C: By stimulating the production of visual pigments in the retina
options.D: By acting as a hormone to control blood glucose levels

explanation: Vitamin E sits inside cell membranes and stops free radicals from destroying delicate fats within the cell structure. [learn more](BMP118_U2_T4#BMP118_U2_T4_h3)

question: What is an early sign of vitamin A deficiency in pregnant women?
explanation: Difficulty seeing in dim light, known as night blindness, is typically the first sign that the body lacks sufficient vitamin A. [learn more](BMP118_U2_T4#BMP118_U2_T4_h4)

question: A newborn baby is bleeding from the umbilical stump and has bruising. Which vitamin deficiency is the midwife likely suspecting?
explanation: Newborns have low vitamin K stores and sterile guts, putting them at risk of bleeding problems unless prophylactic vitamin K is administered. [learn more](BMP118_U2_T4#BMP118_U2_T4_h4)

question: Which fat-soluble vitamin can cause birth defects if taken in high doses during the first trimester?
explanation: Preformed vitamin A in megadoses can cause birth defects when taken during early pregnancy, which is why prenatal supplements must be carefully regulated. [learn more](BMP118_U2_T4#BMP118_U2_T4_h5)

question: Why does high intake of preformed vitamin A carry a risk of birth defects while eating beta-carotene from vegetables does not?

options.A: Plant carotene cannot cross the placental barrier under any circumstance
options.B: Preformed vitamin A destroys all circulating hormones in the placenta
options.C: Beta-carotene is water-soluble and gets immediately excreted through sweat
options.D: The body strictly regulates the conversion of plant carotene into active vitamin A

explanation: The body only converts as much beta-carotene into vitamin A as it needs, preventing the toxic buildup seen with preformed retinol supplements. [learn more](BMP118_U2_T4#BMP118_U2_T4_h5)

question: A pregnant woman at the antenatal clinic asks for an affordable local source of vitamin A. Which Nigerian food item is best to recommend?
explanation: Unrefined red palm oil is an exceptionally rich, culturally accessible local source of provitamin A carotenoids. [learn more](BMP118_U2_T4#BMP118_U2_T4_h6)

question: What is the main reason midwives in Nigeria should encourage diverse local foods instead of high-potency commercial supplements during pregnancy?

options.A: It minimizes the danger of vitamin toxicity while ensuring steady nutrient intake
options.B: Local foods are scientifically proven to cure all congenital malformations
options.C: Pregnant women cannot absorb synthetic vitamins under tropical weather
options.D: Commercial supplements are completely devoid of any fat-soluble vitamins

explanation: Promoting whole foods supplies essential nutrients safely without the risk of hypervitaminosis associated with unmonitored megadoses. [learn more](BMP118_U2_T4#BMP118_U2_T4_h6)
